The size helper shows undefined for values of a terabyte or more.
The web address check accepts script-style addresses, so it should not be used to decide whether a link is safe.

terms.meaning: A small reusable piece of code that does one job.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header note
sections.what: A header comment saying these are shared helper functions for the frontend.
sections.why: Likely reason: tells readers where these helpers belong.

sections.name: formatFileSize
sections.title: Human readable file size
sections.what: Turns a number of bytes into text such as KB, MB, or GB, rounded to two decimals. Zero shows as zero bytes.
sections.why: Likely reason: file sizes are easier to read in KB or MB than as raw byte counts.
sections.watch_out: The unit list stops at GB, so a value of a terabyte or more shows undefined as its unit.

sections.name: formatDate
sections.title: Readable date
sections.what: Turns a date text into a short date such as Jan 5, 2026, in US English.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the date style the same on every screen.
sections.watch_out: Invalid date text shows as Invalid Date, and the US English style is fixed.

sections.name: truncate
sections.title: Shorten long text
sections.what: Cuts text to a set length and adds three dots if it was cut.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps long names from breaking the layout.
sections.watch_out: The cut can land in the middle of a word, and the result is three characters longer than the set length.

sections.name: getFileExtension
sections.title: File extension lookup
sections.what: Returns the letters after the last dot in a file name, such as pdf. A name with no dot returns empty text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the screen uses the type to choose an icon or filter.
sections.watch_out: The calculation is unusual and relies on a number trick, so test it before changing it. It keeps the original capital letters.

sections.name: isValidUrl
sections.title: Web address check
sections.what: Returns true if the text can be read as a web address, and false otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: helps avoid saving broken links.
sections.watch_out: It accepts any address scheme, including script-style addresses, so a true result does not prove a link is safe.

summary: A small set of helper functions that format file sizes and dates, shorten text, read file extensions, and check whether text is a web address.
purpose: Gives the frontend shared helpers so screens show sizes, dates, and names in the same way.
why: Likely reason: avoids repeating the same small formatting code in each screen.
how: Each helper takes one value, does a small calculation or check, and returns text or a yes or no answer. The file does not call the backend and keeps no state.
inputs: A number of bytes, a date as text, a maximum length, a file name, or a piece of text.
outputs: Readable size text, readable date text, shortened text, an extension, or a true or false answer.
risks: Some helpers give odd results at the edges. Sizes of a terabyte or more show as undefined, and the web address check accepts script-style addresses.
debug: If a size shows undefined, check that the value is below one terabyte and is not negative. If a date shows Invalid Date, check the date text format. If a link check passes something odd, remember it only checks that the text parses as a URL.
